The match was dominated by Indonesia, with 19-year-old striker Mitchell Baker, who stands 6'5", scoring five goals alone to dismantle the Bangladesh defense.
Bangladesh managed to score two goals, with Shahriar Emon scoring in the 36th minute and Farhan Ali finding the net in the second-half stoppage time.

Bangladesh ended the tournament without a win, losing all three matches against Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, conceding a total of 13 goals.

headline: Bangladesh suffers heaviest football defeat in 3 years losing 9-2 to Indonesia
summary: Bangladesh's national football team endured a crushing 9-2 loss to Indonesia in their final FIFA ASEAN Cup fixture. The defeat marks their most significant loss in three years, highlighting challenges against higher-ranked opponents.
details: Bangladesh suffered a heavy 9-2 defeat against Indonesia in their final FIFA ASEAN Cup match held in Jakarta. USA-based striker Mitchell Baker was instrumental for Indonesia, scoring five goals. Bangladesh conceded six goals in the first half, struggling to match Indonesia's pace and intensity.

Shahriar Emon scored Bangladesh's first goal in the 36th minute, making it 3-1, but Indonesia quickly responded. By halftime, Bangladesh was trailing 6-1. Despite showing more resilience in the second half, the team conceded three more goals, with Farhaan Ali Wahid scoring Bangladesh's second in stoppage time.

This 9-2 drubbing is Bangladesh's heaviest defeat in three years, surpassing their 7-0 loss to Australia in a World Cup qualifier. Historically, Bangladesh's most significant losses include 9-0 defeats against Japan in 1979 and Iran in 1982.

Coach Thomas Dooley had expressed concerns about a potential heavy defeat before the match, and his fears were realized. Indonesia, ranked 65 places above Bangladesh, fielded a team with Europe-based players and was determined to secure a large win to reach the final.

The match was briefly interrupted by a confrontation between players from both sides. Following the resumption of play, Indonesia scored twice more to seal their victory and secure a spot in the final ahead of Malaysia on goal difference. Goalkeeper Mehedi Hasan Srabon made several crucial saves to prevent an even larger margin of defeat.

Bangladesh had previously lost 3-0 to Malaysia and 1-0 to Singapore in the same group stage. The team had hoped to build on an improved performance against Singapore but ultimately faced a devastating outcome against a stronger Indonesian side.
